question: One carbon carrying a carboxyl group, a nitrogen group, a hydrogen and one distinctive side chain makes an _____, and that side chain decides everything about its role.
questions: Nine of them cannot be built by any human cell, so this kind of _____ has to come from food and is called essential for that reason alone.
Every living thing builds proteins from the left-handed mirror form only, and why an _____ should have that handedness at all is still an unsettled question.
abstract:
An amino acid is a carbon atom bonded to a carboxyl group, an amino group, a hydrogen atom and a distinctive side chain, and the chemistry of that side chain decides what part the molecule plays in a protein. The twenty used in proteins fall into four groups by side chain: ten nonpolar, five polar but uncharged, three basic and two acidic. Nonpolar side chains do not interact with water and tend to end up in the interior of a folded protein, while the polar ones form hydrogen bonds with water and sit on the outside. Cysteine is worth singling out, because the sulfhydryl group on its side chain lets disulfide bonds form between two cysteines and hold a structure together. Nine of the twenty cannot be made by human or other mammalian cells and must come from food: histidine, isoleucine, leucine, lysine, methionine, phenylalanine, threonine, tryptophan and valine.

A further group counts as semi-essential, made by the body ordinarily but needed from the diet during growth, pregnancy and other periods of stress. The twenty are not a hard limit either, and bacteria have been engineered to make non-canonical amino acids and read them into proteins through an expanded genetic code. What is universal is the handedness: every organism builds its proteins from the left-handed mirror form alone, and how that single-handedness arose is still argued over. After an organism dies the handedness slowly decays towards a mixture, so the ratio of right-handed to left-handed forms measures how far the protein has broken down and, where the rate is predictable, how long ago that was. Dating the Schöningen hunting spears that way moved them from roughly 300,000 years old to about 200,000, and with them the record of when hunting became a communal business.
